prior_year_events.impact_description: Costs to remove the Costa Concordia increased during the year, adding a further US$315m to the overall cost (reported as a major marine removal/wreck cost impacting marine reserves).
Further deterioration in the P&I claim for the Rena (grounding in October 2011) increased expected costs (total P&I claim reported at $425m), affecting marine-related reserves.
Hurricane Sandy was identified as a major loss with some open claims remaining and robust reserves set; final quantum may be determined in courts.

named_events.loss_description: Plane disappearance - syndicate agreed to fund 50% of the loss with Hull All Risk insurers paying the other 50%; could pay full claim if malicious act proven.
Loss estimated to cost the syndicate $10.8m gross and $9.8m net; paid quickly as leader on the Malaysian Airlines policy.

data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2014, Syndicate 609 reported opening gross claims outstanding of GBP 378.654m (prior year). A reassessment of claims outstanding on underwriting years 2011 and prior produced an improvement (release) of GBP 41.2m, equivalent to roughly 10.9% of opening gross claims reserves. The managing agent attributes the movement to favourable development on back years. Named loss incidents affecting marine and other portfolios (e.g., Costa Concordia, Rena, Hurricane Sandy) are discussed in the report but the net quantified prior-year release is reported at GBP 41.2m.
raw_causal_phrases: Reassessment of claims outstanding on underwriting years 2011 & prior (2013 - 2010 & prior) resulted in an improvement of GBP 41.2 m (2013 - GBP 28.7m).
The syndicate has continued to benefit from favorable development on the back years that contributed GBP 38.4m to the result.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development figure (GBP 41.2m improvement) taken from Note 2 'Claims Outstanding' narrative. The note explicitly states an improvement but does not explicitly label the figure as 'gross' vs 'net' in the single-sentence narrative; given its placement in the claims outstanding note it is treated as a gross claims movement. No gross claims development triangle was present in the main accounts to cross-check. RITC and the 2012/2011 syndicate merger transactions are present in the underwriting year accounts and could distort development calculations for certain underwriting years; amounts in the report are presented in GBP '000 and have been converted to millions in this JSON.
